transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not wasting your time with something silly, but... well, I'm a building cleaner, and I've been having a little trouble with parts of my job lately. 

It's honestly so embarrassing to admit, but... the thought of seeing a rat has gotten so bad that I just can't do certain tasks anymore. Like going into the trash rooms or the older parts of the building. I know it's silly, right? Because it's just an old building, it's not really dangerous. I know that in my head. But I just... I can't do it, and it's getting in the way of my work. Does that make sense? I really just want to get back to doing a good job and not be a bother to my supervisor.
Is your fear specifically about rats, or does it also happen with other animals or situations?

Oh, no, it's... it's just rats. I'm totally fine with other animals. I mean, I love dogs and cats, and even things like spiders or bugs don't really bother me. It's really just... just rats. I know it sounds so specific and weird, right? I hope that doesn't make it harder for you to help me. I really am trying to be reasonable about it, it's just... that one specific thing that really gets to me. Is that... is that normal for people to just be afraid of one thing like that?
